task: 5.1 — Preserve package artifacts and explicit release commands
status: GREEN for all six acceptance items, verified with real npm pack / npm install runs against the actual repository, not only fixtures. Two of the 17 packages (bitcore-p2p-cash, bitcore-p2p-doge) could not complete their real `prepare: ["build"]` step in this environment because of a pre-existing, already-recorded (Task 1.1) test-suite defect unrelated to packaging -- see preExistingBaselineDefectsNoted. Their manifest and tarball-content checks were still run and passed for real by packing them without that prepare step, and the pre-existing defect is unchanged either way.

modified: packages/crypto-wallet-core/package.json — adds a `files: ["ts_build"]` field (real defect fix, see findings)
packages/bitcore-client/package.json — adds a `files: ["ts_build"]` field (real defect fix, see findings)
packages/bitcore-node/package.json — moves `axios` from devDependencies to dependencies (real defect fix, see findings)
packages/bitcore-wallet-client/package.json — moves `kbpgp` and `request-promise` from devDependencies to dependencies (real defect fix, see findings)
.idea/npm-workspaces/bitcore-acceptance-spec.md — documents the two new commands in section 7

implementation.packBaseline: scripts/workspaces/release-baseline.json records packages/pub's real MODULES selection/order verbatim, including its pre-existing duplicate bitcore-p2p-doge entry, plus one entry per non-private workspace (17, matching package.json's 18 workspaces minus private bitcore-cli) with its directory/name/version/publishConfig and an explicit `prepare` script list -- only the scripts genuinely needed *beyond* the root's own upfront `npm run compile` (which already builds the 7 COMPILE_ORDER packages): the 8 gulp-family packages (bitcore-lib*, bitcore-mnemonic, bitcore-p2p*) need `build` (gulp's default task, which is `test`, not merely a bundling step -- see acceptanceNote), and bitcore-wallet-client needs `build` specifically because its own `compile` script omits the `lint` step that its real `pub` script requires.
implementation.packCjs: scripts/workspaces/pack.cjs (`npm run artifacts:check`) asserts the release-loop selection/order and package-directory set against the baseline, runs `npm run compile` once, then per candidate: runs its recorded prepare scripts, packs via `npm pack --workspace=<name> --pack-destination=<dir> --json`, re-checks the extracted tarball's manifest and required file contents (main/types/bin, bitcore-build's shared karma/wdio configs, wallet-service's real on-disk templates tree), and runs the declared-dependency audit below. Writes `artifacts.json` (name/version/tarball path per package). Never invokes npm publish/version/tag or a package's own `pub` script.
implementation.auditPackedCjs: scripts/workspaces/audit-packed.cjs statically scans each package's own implementation tree (declared entry-point subdirectories plus the package's own top-level files, since several packages declare `main` directly at the root) for non-relative `require`/`import`/`import type(...)` specifiers, and fails when one names a package the manifest does not declare as a dependency/optionalDependency/peerDependency -- independent of whatever the eventual validation consumer happens to have hoisted. A small, explicitly named DOCUMENTED_BASELINE_EXCEPTIONS set (mirroring the engines verifier's own socks5-client exception) carries the one pre-existing, out-of-scope defect found (see findings) so a real future regression is never silently masked by broadening it.
implementation.verifyConsumerCjs: scripts/workspaces/verify-consumer.cjs (`npm run artifacts:consumer -- --artifacts=<destination>/artifacts.json`) installs every listed tarball together into one disposable npm project outside the checkout (so npm cannot silently substitute a registry-published internal package for one under test), confirms each installed package is a real extracted tarball at its candidate version (not a symlink, not resolving back into the checkout), type-checks a small TypeScript consumer against wallet-client's shipped declarations with the repository's own tsc, and runs a small ESM script exercising a representative public API (`new Key()`, from wallet-client) plus a named ESM import of crypto-rpc's `CryptoRpc` export, on Node 22.

findings.defect: crypto-wallet-core and bitcore-client's real `npm pack` (both via `--workspace=` from the root and run directly from inside each package's own directory) silently excluded their entire `ts_build/` compiled output, so the tarball's declared `main`/`types` did not resolve -- confirmed with a real `npm pack --pack-destination=<dir>` and `tar -tzf` on the actual produced tarball, not just the `--json` dry-run summary.
findings.rootCause: Neither package declares a package.json `files` field, so npm falls back to `.gitignore`/`.npmignore` resolution; the root `.gitignore`'s bare `ts_build` entry (matches at any depth) reaches these two specifically, empirically confirmed by removing that one line from a scratch copy of the root `.gitignore` and observing the pack include `ts_build` immediately afterward, then restoring it. The exact per-package mechanism npm-packlist uses to decide which ignore files apply to which workspace (why bitcore-wallet-service/-client/-logging were unaffected despite the same root rule) was not fully reverse-engineered -- not needed, since the fix below is correct regardless of that internal mechanism.
findings.disposition: FIXED: added an explicit `files: ["ts_build"]` to both packages' package.json (README/LICENSE/package.json/declared `bin` are always included by npm regardless of `files`). Re-verified with a real `npm pack --dry-run --json`: both now include `ts_build/src/index.js` and `ts_build/src/index.d.ts`. The currently-published `@bitpay-labs/crypto-wallet-core@11.10.4` on the real npm registry does include `ts_build` (356 files, confirmed via `npm pack @bitpay-labs/crypto-wallet-core@11.10.4 --dry-run`), so this is not evidence of anything already broken for existing consumers -- it is a real risk for the *next* publish from this checkout that this task's own required check ("generated entry points are not lost through .gitignore / .npmignore interaction") exists specifically to catch.

findings.defect: bitcore-node's compiled `build/src/providers/chain-state/external/adapters/{alchemy,moralis}.js` and `.../external/streams/apiStream.js` import `axios`, which was declared only as a devDependency -- an external consumer installing the published package would not receive it and would hit a runtime `Cannot find module` on those code paths.
findings.disposition: FIXED: moved `axios` from devDependencies to dependencies in packages/bitcore-node/package.json (same version, `0.21.1`).

findings.defect: bitcore-wallet-client's compiled `ts_build/src/util/fetchBitpayKeysAndVerify.js` imports `kbpgp` and `request-promise`, both declared only as devDependencies. This file is not reachable from the package's declared public API (src/index.ts never imports it) but does ship in the tarball, so an undocumented deep subpath require of it would still hit a missing-module error for an external consumer.
findings.disposition: FIXED: moved `kbpgp` and `request-promise` from devDependencies to dependencies in packages/bitcore-wallet-client/package.json (same version ranges).

findings.defect: bitcore-wallet-service's compiled `ts_build/src/lib/chain/eth/index.d.ts` and `.../xrp/index.d.ts` contain a bare `import ... from 'src/lib/model'` (and `'src/lib/server'`) specifier. It resolves locally only because the package's own tsconfig sets `baseUrl: "."`; tsc emits that same literal specifier into the shipped declaration file, where it cannot resolve for an external consumer type-checking against the package. The same pattern (not confirmed reachable in the shipped ts_build output) also exists in src/types/chain.d.ts and src/types/expressapp.d.ts.
findings.disposition: NOT FIXED — recorded as an explicit, named, out-of-scope pre-existing baseline defect (scripts/workspaces/audit-packed.cjs's DOCUMENTED_BASELINE_EXCEPTIONS). The fix requires editing application TypeScript source (the actual import specifiers), which is outside Task 5.1's packaging-metadata-only file scope. A human should decide whether/when to fix the source and, once fixed, delete the now-unneeded exception entries (the audit-packed tests would then need updating too, since two of them construct this exact fixture).

findings.defect: packages/pub (the pre-existing release loop) joins each iteration's `npm run pub` to its `cd ..` with `;`, not `&&`, and sets no `set -e`. Confirmed with a real stub-npm run (test/workspaces/pub-entrypoint.test.cjs): a failing `npm run pub` on the very first package still lets the loop continue through every remaining package, and the overall script still exits 0.
findings.disposition: NOT FIXED — recorded as an explicit, out-of-scope pre-existing baseline defect, following the same disposition the plan already gives the release loop's other pre-existing defect (the duplicate P2P Doge entry): recorded as baseline metadata, repair kept as a separate follow-up, since packages/pub's own file scope for this task was verification ("Verify the existing release entry point still routes into package scripts using a stub npm process"), not repair of its failure-handling behavior.

preExistingBaselineDefectsNoted.defect: bitcore-p2p-cash and bitcore-p2p-doge's own `npm run build` (gulp's default task, which really runs their full test suite, not a bundling step) each fail two tests: `Peer create instance setting a network` (`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'should')`, a real, package-specific test-source bug -- these two forks never picked up a workaround the base bitcore-p2p package's own test file already has, at the same test) and `Peer version/subversion settings respected` (`AggregateError [ECONNREFUSED]`, a real live-peer network prerequisite that is not provisioned in this environment).
preExistingBaselineDefectsNoted.evidence: Reproduced live in this session (log excerpts in the session transcript); the bitcore-p2p-cash instance of this exact failure was already recorded before this task, in .idea/npm-workspaces/evidence-1.1/consumer-regressions/p2p-cash.log, confirming it predates this migration and this task's changes.
preExistingBaselineDefectsNoted.impact: Blocks `npm run artifacts:check` from completing a single uninterrupted run today: the tool's fail-fast design (a required behavior -- "propagates failures") correctly stops at the first prepare-script failure it hits, which is bitcore-p2p-cash (alphabetically before bitcore-p2p-doge in scripts/workspaces/release-baseline.json). Both packages' manifest and tarball-content checks were still verified for real in this task by packing them without their `prepare` step (their `main`/`lib` are already-committed, uncompiled JS, so `build` changes nothing about the tarball's content, only whether their tests get re-run) -- see implementation notes.
preExistingBaselineDefectsNoted.disposition: NOT FIXED — recording and running around this defect is as far as this task's scope goes. Actually fixing bitcore-p2p-cash/-doge's test suites (or provisioning the live peer their second failing test needs) belongs to whatever task owns the "P2P regression" gate (bitcore-migration-plan.md Task 5.3's acceptance matrix), not this one.

evidence.realFullRunOf17: A real, uninterrupted `node scripts/workspaces/pack.cjs --destination=<dir>` ran to completion through 10 of 17 packages (bitcore-build, bitcore-client, bitcore-lib, bitcore-lib-cash, bitcore-lib-doge, bitcore-lib-ltc, bitcore-logging, bitcore-mnemonic, bitcore-node, bitcore-p2p) before stopping at bitcore-p2p-cash's real, pre-existing build failure (see preExistingBaselineDefectsNoted). checkManifest already ran successfully for all 17 real package.json manifests before that point, since that loop runs before the per-candidate build/pack loop.
evidence.remainingPackagesVerifiedSeparately: The remaining packages not reached by the run above were each independently packed and checked for real, reusing the exact same exported checkManifest/checkContents/audit functions: bitcore-tss, bitcore-wallet-client (including its real `build` step: tsc + eslint lint), bitcore-wallet-service (surfacing exactly the two documented wallet-service exceptions and no unexpected failures), crypto-rpc, and crypto-wallet-core all passed in full, including their real prepare/build steps. bitcore-p2p-cash and bitcore-p2p-doge were packed and manifest/content-checked without their `prepare: ["build"]` step (see preExistingBaselineDefectsNoted for why), and passed. `audit()` was additionally run directly (no packing needed) against all 17 real package directories with zero unexpected failures.
evidence.externalConsumer: `node scripts/workspaces/verify-consumer.cjs --artifacts=<dir>/artifacts.json --destination=<dir2>` ran to completion (exit 0) against the 15 real tarballs produced above, in a disposable npm project outside the checkout: `npm install` pulled 2364 real packages (including native builds: leveldown, secp256k1, bcrypt); every candidate resolved to its real extracted tarball at the expected version, none as a symlink or resolving back into the checkout; the repository's own tsc type-checked a small consumer against wallet-client's shipped declarations (target ES2022, `skipLibCheck: false`) with exit 0; the Node runtime check constructed a real `Key()` (wallet-client's representative public API, exercising its own real dependency closure: bitcore-mnemonic, bitcore-tss, crypto-wallet-core) and performed a real named ESM import of crypto-rpc's `CryptoRpc` export.
evidence.unitTests: `node --test test/workspaces/*.test.cjs` — 117 passing, 0 failing (24 new: 12 in audit-packed.test.cjs, 12 in pack.test.cjs and pub-entrypoint.test.cjs combined; 93 pre-existing, unaffected).
evidence.lint: `npx eslint scripts/workspaces/ test/workspaces/` — 0 errors (123 warnings, all the pre-existing `@typescript-eslint/no-require-imports` pattern already present throughout this directory's other committed .cjs files).
